entries.narrative: MF-030 closes a silent failure of the epic's binding complexity gate. analyze_complexity.py read one .tla file and stopped at EXTENDS, so on the decomposed architecture SKILL.md mandates it scored only the declarations literally present in the analyzed file. The error is never conservative: missing variables only ever shrink the product bound, so the gate failed toward PASS on exactly the shape the skill requires. MF-023 measured External reporting bound = 1 over 2 of 9 variables from this. The fix is a partial module resolver (resolve_module) that follows EXTENDS through the hierarchy and unions VARIABLES, CONSTANTS, and the top-level definitions carrying TypeInvariant/Init/actions, base-first with the extending module overriding inherited names. Standard TLA+ library modules (Naturals, Integers, Reals, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags, TLC, Json) declare no VARIABLES the bound reads and are skipped rather than resolved to a file. Every construct the resolver cannot model FAILS CLOSED with a named error rather than under-reporting: INSTANCE / named and unnamed instantiation, WITH substitution, and parameterized instantiation via UnsupportedModuleConstructError; LOCAL via the same; and an EXTENDS naming a non-standard module with no findable .tla via UnresolvedExtendsError. analyze() propagates these; run() and gate_report() catch them and fail closed (nonzero / gate FAIL with the reason). This honours references/architecture_tractability.md "No Degenerate Escapes": when a model cannot be resolved, write the failure, not a smaller number. Measured alternatives and the self-scrutiny check: the risk flagged for this ticket was a resolver that appears to work on a model where the extended declarations do not matter to the bound. The regression fixture is deliberately the opposite -- Channel EXTENDS Counter, where the EXTENDED module carries the only bound-bearing variable (tick in 0..3) and the extending module adds only an unconstrained channel variable. Pre-fix the analyzer reports variables= ['emitted'], bound=1, Bump absent; post-fix variables={tick,emitted}, bound=4, Bump present. The number moves 1->4 and the assertions were run against the HEAD analyzer to confirm they fail pre-fix. Shipped example re-measured (examples/distributed_history, External EXTENDS Internal EXTENDS Core, no TypeInvariant so bound is 1 both ways): its verdict stays FAIL but the diagnosis is corrected from a spurious "C2 {responses} touched by 9 actions" (an artifact of seeing only External's 4 variables) to the true "C1 {accounts,carts,orders, responses} touched by 13 actions" over all 10 variables, with named port-crossing actions and modularity 0.000 -> 0.230. That corrected figure is relevant to MF-037 and the ticket-workflow example: any downstream copy of the old 9-action number is stale. entries.narrative: MF-036 makes the complexity check ADVISORY. A probe built a plain 5-variable, 10-command god-object CLI (recorded under results/probe/GodObjectCli.tla) and ran `analyze complexity`; it HARD-FAILED with "component C1 is touched by 10 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8" (exit 1). Any program with more than eight commands over shared state failed the same way -- i.e. most real programs. Per owner direction 2026-07-20 and references/architecture_tractability.md ("Advisory, Not Blocking"), complexity is a scanner, not a gate. What changed (scripts only, zero TLA delta): (1) Every complexity threshold breach -- state-space bound, component variables, component actions, and the TLC distinct-states check -- is now an advisory WARNING that names the component/variable/action and RECOMMENDS a concrete move (e.g. "split the densest state <v> into its own component"). `analyze complexity` exits 0 whenever it can analyze the model; it exits nonzero ONLY when it CANNOT analyze it (the MF-030 fail-closed on an unresolved EXTENDS/INSTANCE hierarchy). "I could not measure this" stays an error; "this is complex" is now a finding. (2) Case generation no longer refuses above threshold. `enforce_complexity_gate` became `advise_complexity`: it prints the warnings and proceeds. The `--allow-over-budget` override was removed entirely -- there is no gate left to override. (3) Frame-condition accuracy fix: `v' = v` (the written-out form of UNCHANGED) was counted as a read AND a write, so every variable an action leaves alone showed as coupled to it. It is now stripped. On the GodObjectCli probe this drops the over-reported god-state from all five variables at 10/10 to the real coupling (only the shared `status` at 10/10; the four domain vars at 3/3/2/2), and the R/W interaction graph de-densifies from the complete graph (10 edges) to a star (4 edges).
